---
title: "Build a Terminal UI in R with termr"
description: "Install termr, compose a terminal form in R, handle keyboard events, and verify the app with a headless test."
---

termr is a reactive terminal user interface (TUI) framework for R. Applications
combine a widget tree, layouts, event handlers and keyboard bindings. This
tutorial uses stable exported APIs and the verified basic application recipe.

## Install termr

Use R 4.1 or newer. Install the recommended stable release from
[CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=termr):

```r
install.packages("termr")
```

For the R-universe alternative, GitHub development installation, and platform
limits, see the [installation guide](../index.html#installation) and
[platform matrix](https://github.com/menshikovs/termr/blob/main/docs/platform-testing.md).

## Compose your first application

Save the following chunk as `basic-app.R`. It constructs the app without
starting terminal input, so the same object can be tested headlessly.

```{r basic-app}
library(termr)

ui <- vertical(
  label("What is your name?"),
  input(id = "name", placeholder = "Your name"),
  button("Say hello", id = "hello", variant = "primary"),
  label("", id = "output")
)

application <- app(
  ui,
  on("button.pressed", "#hello", function(event, app) {
    name <- app$query_one("#name")$value
    app$query_one("#output")$update(paste("Hello,", name))
  }),
  bind("escape", "quit")
)
```

`vertical()` stacks the widgets. Use `horizontal()` for a row or
`grid_layout()` for a grid. `id` identifies a widget for selectors such as
`#name`; the button event handler reads the input's `$value` and updates the
output label. `bind()` connects a key to an action.

## Run in a real terminal

```sh
Rscript -e "source('basic-app.R'); termr::run(application)"
```

Type a name, press Tab to focus the button, then Enter. Escape quits. Use a
real terminal or IDE terminal tab; an IDE console cannot host the full-screen
app. Handled exits restore the terminal, while forced process termination
cannot guarantee cleanup.

## Verify without a terminal

After sourcing `basic-app.R` in a fresh R session, run:

```{r verify-basic-app}
verify_greeting <- function() {
  pilot <- test_app(application, width = 40, height = 10)
  on.exit(pilot$stop(), add = TRUE)
  pilot$type("Ada")
  pilot$press("tab", "enter")
  stopifnot(identical(pilot$query_one("#output")$text, "Hello, Ada"))
  stopifnot(any(grepl("Hello, Ada", pilot$screen_text(), fixed = TRUE)))
}
verify_greeting()
```

This chunk executes during the website build. It checks keyboard handling,
widget state and rendered text through the normal event loop.
